title: Automox Overview
description:
## Automox

This dashboard provides an overview of your Automox organizations: device inventory, patch backlog, policy compliance, devices needing attention and each policy's latest run, alongside Automox console activity and audit logs.

Clone this template to make changes and add your own graphs and widgets.

definition.content:
An overview of your Automox device inventory, patch backlog, policy compliance, devices needing attention and each policy's latest run, alongside Automox console activity and audit logs.

Organization, compliance and needs-attention readings refresh every few minutes. Per-device inventory and patch counts are collected **twice a day**.

**Filters:** *organization_id*, *server_group_id*, *device*, *policy*, *failing_device* and *failing_policy* narrow the display.

Logs are under `source:automox`, and `@evt.category` names the stream:

- `events`: devices added and removed, patch outcomes, policy actions and user changes
- `audit`: the Automox audit trail, in OCSF

Policy runs are metrics: `automox.policy_run.*` reports each policy's latest run.

**References**
- [Automox documentation](https://docs.automox.com/)
- [Automox OCSF Schema](https://docs.automox.com/product/Developer/OCSF_Schema_Overview.htm)

`automox.device.info` reports one series per device, tagged with: name, OS, agent version and group. The state is a gauge each, 1 or 0: `automox.device.connected`, `ready`, `policy_compliant`, `managed`, `needs_reboot`, `needs_attention`, `is_compatible` and `last_scan_failed`. All are collected twice a day.
**Pending patches** are the patches Automox considers due on each device. **Outstanding packages** count everything available, by severity. Collected twice a day.

Device counts per policy in each state. A device assigned to several policies is counted once per policy, so totals are device-policy pairs and will not match the fleet size or the console's Policy Compliant Devices widget.

The console's Device Troubleshooting report. **Devices** counts non-compliant devices; **packages** counts the outstanding packages on them, by severity. A failing policy carries its worst package severity. A failing device's state is 1 or 0 per device so the policy filter narrows only Failing Policies.
`@evt.category:events` represents devices added and removed, patches applied or failed, policy actions and user changes.
Each policy's latest run: devices `pending`, `success` and `failed`, and the run's `device_count`, tagged `policy_id`, `policy_name` and `org_uuid`.

`@evt.category:audit` is the audit trail: sign-ins, roles, 2FA and API keys, groups, policies and device management. Automox [emits these records in OCSF 1.1.0](https://docs.automox.com/product/Developer/OCSF_Schema_Overview.htm) and the Datadog pipeline converts them to OCSF 1.5.0.
